## Goal
Issue and board bookkeeping for a ticket runs through one tested script, `tools/ticket.sh start|review|ready|done|file`, so each step produces the same result every time (no duplicate `Branch:` lines, no second comment on a re-run), and the ticket-flow skill and the bookkeeping steps call it instead of assembling `gh` calls. The ticket also adds the stubbed-`gh` harness the follow-up scripts reuse.

## Context and decisions relied on
- Decision to script the recurring bookkeeping (preset commands instead of re-deriving `gh` calls) is recorded in `https://github.com/rodgallert/Elysium/issues/62#issuecomment-6961508247`; the sprint split it into three tickets (this one, then `pr.sh`, then `wt.sh`) with the harness and the account guard here.
- The ticket-flow steps it implements are in `.claude/skills/ticket-flow/SKILL.md` (`file`, `start`, `review`, `done`) and `Docs/workflow.md` ("Specs and tests" rule 4: spec approval and the approval-time check; "Sprints"). Board moves reuse `tools/board.sh`; board fields reuse `tools/board-field.sh`.
- Existing stub style and fixture-test style: `tools/tests/stubs/gh` and `tools/tests/release-tools.sh` (temporary directory only, guard that refuses to run elsewhere).
- Decisions specific to this ticket (recorded in `https://github.com/rodgallert/Elysium/issues/62#issuecomment-6961508247`): the spec's approval time is read from the issue body's edit history through GraphQL `userContentEdits` (paginated), never from `updatedAt` (labels and comments move it); the script uses only the `rodgallert` account's token and never switches accounts; `ready` means the move to **Ready to Merge**.
- The call wrapper (token, retries, timeout, number validation) lives in one sourced file under `tools/`, so `pr.sh` and `wt.sh` reuse it.
- Commands: `ticket.sh start <n>`, `review <n> <pr>`, `ready <n>`, `done <n>`, `file --title <t> --type <type> --epic <n> [--milestone <m>] --body-file <file>`. Every `gh` call is made with `GH_TOKEN` set from the owner's login; titles and bodies go through `--body-file` or stdin, never into a command line.

A `GH_TOKEN` already in the environment is accepted only if `gh api user -q .login` returns `rodgallert`.

     - **#70-AC1.2 boundaries:** `1` and `9999999` accepted, `10000000` rejected.
     - **#70-AC1.3 state and lifecycle:** n/a: argument checks run before any state is read.
     - **#70-AC1.4 time:** n/a: no clock involved.
     - **#70-AC1.5 concurrency:** n/a: covered by AC2.5.
     - **#70-AC1.6 partial failure:** `gh auth token --user rodgallert` failing exits 1 before any call; `gh` missing exits 1 with one line.
     - **#70-AC1.7 retries and idempotence:** n/a: guards have no effect to repeat.
     - **#70-AC1.8 permissions:** active account `gambiarrista-dll` in the stub: its token is never used (a stub `gh` that fails any call carrying that token proves it); a preset `GH_TOKEN` of another login is refused.
     - **#70-AC1.9 environment differences:** `gh` below the minimum version exits 1; `jq` absent exits 1; the script runs under the CI Ubuntu `bash` and the local Fedora `bash` 5 (the test file starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bash`).
     - **#70-AC1.10 observability:** no output of the script, with or without `set -x` in the caller and when a stub `gh` fails, contains `gho_`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_` or the value of `GH_TOKEN` (the test greps stdout and stderr of every case).
2. **#70-AC2:** `start <n>` is idempotent and ordered. On an open issue whose spec is approved (AC3) and which is not already started it: creates the branch once with `gh issue develop`, appends exactly one `Branch: <branch>` line to the body, moves the board to **In progress**, assigns the issue to the account, and posts one comment `Started on branch <branch>.`. A second `start` of the same issue changes nothing, prints `already started on <branch>` and exits 0.
   - **Edge cases and failure paths.**
     - **#70-AC2.1 inputs:** a body that already has a `Branch:` line gets no second one; a body with `Branch:` text inside a code fence or prose is not mistaken for the line (only a line starting with `Branch: ` at the end of the body counts).
     - **#70-AC2.2 boundaries:** an issue with an empty body fails the spec gate (AC3) with exit 1, not a crash.
     - **#70-AC2.3 state and lifecycle:** `start` on a closed issue, a merged PR's issue, or an issue already **In progress** with a branch is a no-op, exit 0, `already`; a ticket missing its `type: ` label exits 1 naming it.
     - **#70-AC2.4 time:** n/a: ordering is by steps, not time; the 30 s call timeout is tested in AC5.4.
     - **#70-AC2.5 concurrency:** two `start` processes on one issue at once produce exactly one `gh issue develop` call (a per-issue lock on a file descriptor; the second sees the branch and reports `already`).
     - **#70-AC2.6 partial failure:** branch created, board move fails (stub returns 502 then 200): the script retries per AC5, and a re-run after a final failure completes the remaining steps with no second branch, no second `Branch:` line and no second comment.
     - **#70-AC2.7 retries and idempotence:** second run: zero writes (the stub counts `issue develop`, `issue edit`, `issue comment` and board calls and all are 0).
     - **#70-AC2.8 permissions:** covered by AC1.8.
     - **#70-AC2.9 environment differences:** the branch name follows `<type>/p<n>-<slug>` for roadmap tasks and `<type>/<slug>` for others, with the slug lower-case `[a-z0-9-]` only.
     - **#70-AC2.10 observability:** each step prints one line (`branch: ...`, `board: In progress`, `comment: posted|already`); a failure names the step.
3. **#70-AC3:** The spec gate. `start` refuses (exit 1, ticket left as it is, one line saying what is missing) unless the body has an `Approved: <comment link>` line whose comment is `Issue last edited <time>` and `<time>` is not earlier than the last edit to a spec section (Goal through Out of scope). The last spec edit time is read from the issue's GraphQL `userContentEdits` (`createdAt`, newest first, `first: 100`, followed through `pageInfo.endCursor` until `hasNextPage` is false); an edit whose diff touches only the `Epic:`, `Approved:`, `Branch:` or `PR:` lines is ignored. An empty `userContentEdits` means the body was never edited, so the body is the approved version and its creation time is the reference. `updatedAt` is never used, and never as a fallback. Times are compared as UTC ISO-8601 strings (`Z` suffix).
   - **Edge cases and failure paths.**
     - **#70-AC3.1 inputs:** an `Approved:` line pointing at another issue's comment, at a comment whose text is not `Issue last edited <time>`, or at a non-URL is refused; a malformed `<time>` is refused.
     - **#70-AC3.2 boundaries:** an edit exactly at the approval time passes; one second later fails; 100 edits on one page and 101 (second page) both give the right last edit.
     - **#70-AC3.3 state and lifecycle:** a body edited only on `Branch:` after approval passes; an edit to the criteria after approval fails with the line "needs approval again"; a spec-change comment alone (no body edit) does not move the reference.
     - **#70-AC3.4 time:** a label change or a comment after approval moves `updatedAt` and must not fail the gate (stub returns a later `updatedAt` and the test still passes); time zones other than `Z` in stub data are normalised or rejected, never compared as text.
     - **#70-AC3.5 concurrency:** n/a: the gate is a read.
     - **#70-AC3.6 partial failure:** the GraphQL call failing (5xx, timeout) after retries exits 1 and never falls back to `updatedAt`; a page 2 failing does not accept the partial list.
     - **#70-AC3.7 retries and idempotence:** n/a: a read has no effect to repeat.
     - **#70-AC3.8 permissions:** covered by AC1.8.
     - **#70-AC3.9 environment differences:** the GraphQL query is the same under the stub and the real `gh api graphql` (the test compares the query text the script sends with a fixture).
     - **#70-AC3.10 observability:** the refusal names the missing item (`no Approved: line`, `approval older than edit at <time>`, `edit history unreadable`).
4. **#70-AC4:** `review`, `ready`, `done` and `file`. `review <n> <pr>` adds one `PR: #<pr>` line, moves the board to **In review** and posts `In review: #<pr>.` once. `ready <n>` moves the board to **Ready to Merge** only when the issue has a `PR:` line. `done <n>` moves the board to **Done**, closes the issue with `Done in #<pr>.` if the merge did not close it, and posts that comment once. `file` creates the issue from `--body-file` with the `ticket` and `type: <type>` labels and the milestone, keeps `Epic: #<n>` as the first line, then edits the body to replace every `#70-AC` placeholder (`70`) with the new number and prints the issue number and URL.
   - **Edge cases and failure paths.**
     - **#70-AC4.1 inputs:** `file` with a body missing the first-line `Epic: #<n>`, an unknown type, or a body that still contains `70` after replacement exits 1 and, when the issue was already created, says so with its number.
     - **#70-AC4.2 boundaries:** a body with no placeholders is created as is; a body with 200 placeholders has all replaced.
     - **#70-AC4.3 state and lifecycle:** `review` on a closed issue or with a second, different PR number refuses (exit 1) rather than stacking `PR:` lines; `ready` without a `PR:` line exits 1; `done` on an issue that is open with no merged PR exits 1.
     - **#70-AC4.4 time:** n/a: no time rules beyond AC5.
     - **#70-AC4.5 concurrency:** two `done` runs at once post one comment (the comment marker line is checked before posting, under the same per-issue lock).
     - **#70-AC4.6 partial failure:** board API times out after the comment was posted: a retry or re-run posts no second comment (a hidden marker line identifies the script's comments); `file` creating the issue and then failing to edit the body is re-runnable by number.
     - **#70-AC4.7 retries and idempotence:** `done` twice posts one comment and closes once; `review` twice with the same PR changes nothing.
     - **#70-AC4.8 permissions:** covered by AC1.8.
     - **#70-AC4.9 environment differences:** n/a: no environment-specific behaviour beyond AC1.9.
     - **#70-AC4.10 observability:** each command prints one line per step and a final `ok` or the failed step.
5. **#70-AC5:** Failure handling against GitHub. A 5xx, a secondary rate limit (403 with `Retry-After`) or a primary rate limit (403 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`) is retried up to 3 times (backoff 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, or the `Retry-After` value) and then exits non-zero naming the failed step; a 404 is reported as "not found", and a rate limit is never reported as "not found". Every `gh` call is wrapped in a 30 s timeout. The backoff sleep and the timeout come from variables the test overrides (`TICKET_SLEEP`, `TICKET_TIMEOUT`), so tests do not wait.
   - **Edge cases and failure paths.**
     - **#70-AC5.1 inputs:** a `Retry-After` of `abc` or a negative number falls back to the default backoff; one above 60 s caps at 60 s.
     - **#70-AC5.2 boundaries:** failing 3 times then succeeding on the 4th attempt succeeds; failing 4 times exits non-zero with the step named.
     - **#70-AC5.3 state and lifecycle:** a run stopped after the board move and before the comment resumes safely on the next run (AC2.6).
     - **#70-AC5.4 time:** a stub `gh` that hangs is killed after the timeout and counted as a failed attempt.
     - **#70-AC5.5 concurrency:** two scripts on the same issue, one rate-limited: the other is unaffected and no step runs twice.
     - **#70-AC5.6 partial failure:** `gh` 502 on the Nth call of a `start`, for each N from 1 to the last: the exit is non-zero, and a re-run ends in the same final state as an uninterrupted run (asserted on the stub's recorded state).
     - **#70-AC5.7 retries and idempotence:** retried writes never duplicate (checked by the stub's write counts).
     - **#70-AC5.8 permissions:** a 403 that is a permission error (not a rate limit) is not retried and says so.
     - **#70-AC5.9 environment differences:** `jq` features used exist in jq 1.6 (the test runs the filters on 1.6 when available, else notes it).
     - **#70-AC5.10 observability:** the failure line names the step and the HTTP status, never the token or the request body.
6. **#70-AC6:** The skill and the ticket-flow steps use it. `.claude/skills/ticket-flow/SKILL.md` (`file`, `start`, `review`, `done` steps) and `Docs/workflow.md` tell whoever does the bookkeeping to run `tools/ticket.sh <command>` instead of the raw `gh` sequences, state that the script is the only place the approval time and the spec gate are computed, and keep the manual fallback described only as "if the script fails, say so and stop"; `tools/tests/ticket-tools.sh` is listed wherever the repository lists its tool tests.
   - **Edge cases and failure paths.**
     - **#70-AC6.1 inputs:** n/a: documentation.
     - **#70-AC6.2 boundaries:** n/a: documentation.
     - **#70-AC6.3 state and lifecycle:** the documented steps and the script's steps match one to one (a grep test lists the script's commands and checks each appears in the skill).
     - **#70-AC6.4 time:** n/a: documentation.
     - **#70-AC6.5 concurrency:** n/a: documentation.
     - **#70-AC6.6 partial failure:** the docs say what to do when a step fails: stop and report, never switch accounts.
     - **#70-AC6.7 retries and idempotence:** the docs say a re-run is safe.
     - **#70-AC6.8 permissions:** the docs repeat "never `gh auth switch`".
     - **#70-AC6.9 environment differences:** n/a: documentation.
     - **#70-AC6.10 observability:** n/a: documentation.

## Contracts
None. (The script reads GitHub's GraphQL API and `gh`'s documented JSON; its own interface is the usage text and exit codes: 0 done or already done, 1 failure, 2 usage.)

## Test plan
| Criterion | Level | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| #70-AC1 | integration (stubbed `gh`, shell) | `tools/tests/stubs/gh` extended to record every call and its token; fixture temporary directory only (the test refuses to run elsewhere) |
| #70-AC2 | integration | stub with state (issue body, branches, board, comments); two parallel processes for AC2.5 |
| #70-AC3 | integration | stub returning `userContentEdits` pages (empty, 1 page, 101 edits, a failing page 2), a later `updatedAt` |
| #70-AC4 | integration | same stub; fault injection by stub failing the Nth call |
| #70-AC5 | integration | stub with 5xx, 403 variants and a hanging call; `TICKET_SLEEP=0`, `TICKET_TIMEOUT=1` |
| #70-AC6 | lint, read-through | grep test of skill text against the script's command list; `shellcheck` on the script and test file |

The first commit adds `tools/tests/ticket-tools.sh` failing against a stub `tools/ticket.sh` that exits 1, each case citing its id in a comment line or function name; later commits make them pass.

## Manual check for the PO
1. On a scratch issue (filed by `ticket.sh file`), run `tools/ticket.sh start <n>` on one that has no `Approved:` line (expected: exit 1, `no Approved: line`, no branch created).
2. Approve it (add the comment and `Approved:` line), run `start <n>` (expected: one branch, `Branch:` line, board **In progress**, one comment), then run it again (expected: `already started on <branch>`, exit 0, no new comment).
3. Edit a criterion of the scratch issue after approval and run `start` on a fresh scratch copy (expected: refused, `approval older than edit at <time>`).
4. Run `tools/ticket.sh start 0` and `tools/ticket.sh start 007` (expected: exit 2, usage line); with `GH_TOKEN` of another account exported, run any command (expected: refused).
5. Run `tools/ticket.sh done <n>` twice (expected: one comment).

## Out of scope
- `pr.sh` (status and verdict): its own ticket in this sprint. `wt.sh` (add and rm): its own ticket in this sprint.
- `ticket.sh` commands for epics, sprints and releases (filed by hand): not planned; spec changes to `Docs/workflow.md` rules: none needed.
- Choosing which model runs the bookkeeper: not part of this ticket.

## Spec approval
The PO approves this spec; an `Approved: <link to the approval comment>` line is added here when they do. The `Epic:`, `Approved:`, `Branch:` and `PR:` lines are bookkeeping; an edit to any section from Goal to Out of scope after approval needs approval again, and every change to the criteria is also recorded as a `Spec change:` comment.

## Goal
Issue and board bookkeeping for a ticket runs through one tested script, `tools/ticket.sh start|review|ready|done|file`, so each step produces the same result every time (no duplicate `Branch:` lines, no second comment on a re-run), and the ticket-flow skill and the bookkeeping steps call it instead of assembling `gh` calls. The ticket also adds the stubbed-`gh` harness the follow-up scripts reuse.

## Context and decisions relied on
